answer: Because the anchor forfeiture is applied at exit, the signal ledger totals each burn, and the lantern audit records the amount lost per key. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 58% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and hence nobody profits from it. An operator that moves capital between 259 aliases thus destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 2 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
